 Dhamtari Leads in Construction of Girls’ Toilets under VB-G Ramji Yojana 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh has emerged as the first district in the state in the construction of girls’ toilets in schools under the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G Ramji) Yojana .   
 Key Points   
 Progress: Construction of girls’ toilets has been completed in eight schools in the district.   
 Target: A total of 335 girls’ toilets are targeted for construction across Dhamtari district.   
 First Toilet: The district's first girls’ toilet was constructed at the primary school in Dhuma Gram Panchayat, Kurud block .   
 Inauguration: The first toilet was inaugurated on 2 October 2026 , on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti .   
 Theme: The initiative carries the message “My Daughter, My Self-Respect” , highlighting the dignity, privacy and safety of girls.   
 Construction Cost: ₹4.30 lakh was approved for the girls’ toilet at Kotgaon School during the financial year 2026–27 .   
 Objective: The initiative aims to improve girls’ health, hygiene, privacy, dignity and regular school attendance .   
  VB-G RAM G:    
 Employment Guarantee: It provides an enhanced statutory wage employment guarantee of 125 days per financial year   
 Funding: It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS)    
 For most states , the cost is shared in a 60:40 ratio between the Centre and the State Governments.   
 For Northeastern and Himalayan states , the funding ratio is 90:10 .   
 For Union Territories without legislatures , the scheme is funded entirely by the Central Government (100%).   
 Read More: Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G Ramji) Yojana

 Three Chhattisgarh Cities Selected for National Cleanliness Awards 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 Three cities of Chhattisgarh — Raipur, Bilaspur and Bilha — have been selected for national awards under Swachh Survekshan 2025–26 . President Droupadi Murmu is scheduled to confer the awards at a ceremony at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, on 11 November 2026 .   
 Key Points:   
 Cities Selected for National Recognition   
 Raipur: The capital city of Chhattisgarh has been selected for recognition under the national cleanliness assessment.   
 Bilaspur: The city has also secured a place among the selected urban bodies.   
 Bilha: The inclusion of Bilha highlights the participation of smaller urban centres in improving sanitation and cleanliness.   
 Recognition: The selection acknowledges the efforts of municipal bodies, sanitation workers and citizens in maintaining urban cleanliness.   
 Swachh Survekshan 2025–26   
 Implementing Ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).   
 Nature: It is a nationwide cleanliness assessment of urban local bodies.   
 Edition: The 2025–26 assessment is the 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan.   
 Theme: “New initiative of cleanliness – extend your hands, do cleanliness together.”   
 Objective: To encourage cities to improve sanitation systems and make cleanliness a collective responsibility.   
 Assessment focus: The initiative promotes improved waste management, sanitation infrastructure, public participation and cleanliness practices.   
 Role of Safai Mitras and Citizen Participation   
 Safai Mitras: Sanitation workers play a vital role in maintaining public spaces, collecting waste and ensuring cleanliness.   
 Recognition: The award ceremony will give special importance to Safai Mitras and field-level sanitation personnel.   
 Representation: Delegations from selected cities are expected to include sanitation workers, sanitation inspectors, supervisors, engineers and mission staff.   
 Community participation: Citizens are encouraged to treat cleanliness as a shared responsibility rather than merely a government programme.   
 Significance of the Recognition   
 Urban Governance: Encourages municipal bodies to improve sanitation planning and service delivery.   
 Public Health: Better waste management and sanitation help reduce environmental and health risks.   
 Dignity of Sanitation Workers: Recognises the contribution of frontline sanitation personnel.   
 Competitive Federalism: Encourages cities and states to improve their cleanliness performance through national-level assessment.   
 Behavioural Change: Promotes cleanliness as an everyday civic responsibility.

 Mogging’ Named Collins Dictionary’s Word of the Year 2026 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 Collins Dictionary has named ‘Mogging’ as its Word of the Year 2026 , following a 210% increase in its usage during the year.    
 Key Points   
 Meaning: Mogging means to outshine, outperform or overshadow someone or something .   
 Origin: The term originated in bodybuilding culture and is believed to have been derived from AMOG (Alpha Male of the Group) .   
 Evolution: It first appeared around 2016 as a noun , referring to the most physically dominant man in a gym, and later evolved into the verb ‘mog’ .   
 Popularisation: The term has gained popularity among Generation Z and Generation Alpha and is increasingly used in online and everyday conversations.   
 Word of the Year 2025: Collins Dictionary selected ‘Vibe Coding’ as its Word of the Year 2025. It refers to creating applications or websites by describing requirements to an AI tool rather than manually writing code.   
 Selection Process: Collins Dictionary monitors language usage through various sources, including social media , analysing both the frequency and patterns of word usage.

 Bahamas Joins International Solar Alliance as 116th Member 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The Commonwealth of The Bahamas has joined the International Solar Alliance (ISA) as its 116th member country . The Instrument of Accession to the ISA Framework Agreement was handed over during the Ninth Session of the ISA Assembly in New Delhi.   
 Key Points:   
 Bahamas' Accession to ISA   
 New Member: The Bahamas became the 116th member of the International Solar Alliance.   
 Date and Venue: The accession took place in November 2026 on the sidelines of the Ninth Session of the ISA Assembly in New Delhi.   
 Representative of the Bahamas: Peter Nicholas Symonette Jr. , High Commissioner of the Bahamas, handed over the Instrument of Accession.   
 Recipient: The document was received by P. S. Gangadhar , Joint Secretary (Economic Diplomacy) and Head of Depository.   
 About the International Solar Alliance (ISA)   
 Establishment: The ISA was jointly launched by India and France in 2015 during the 21st Conference of the Parties (COP21) to the UNFCCC in Paris.   
 Nature: It is an international intergovernmental organisation focused on promoting solar energy deployment.   
 Headquarters: Gurugram, Haryana, India.   
 Framework Agreement: The ISA Framework Agreement entered into force on 6 December 2017 .   
 Membership: The Bahamas' accession increased the alliance's membership to 116 countries .   
 Objectives and Focus Areas of ISA   
 Solar Energy Deployment: Accelerate the adoption of affordable, reliable and sustainable solar energy.   
 Investment Mobilisation: Facilitate investment and reduce the cost of financing solar energy projects.   
 Technology Cooperation: Promote the sharing of solar technologies, knowledge and best practices.   
 Energy Access: Support solar-powered solutions in areas with limited access to reliable electricity.   
 Energy Security: Help countries diversify their energy sources and reduce dependence on fossil fuels.   
 India's Role in Global Solar Cooperation   
 Founding Role: India is a co-founder of the ISA along with France.   
 Global Leadership: The alliance reflects India's efforts to promote renewable energy and international climate cooperation.   
 International Platform: ISA supports collaboration among member countries to expand solar energy deployment, particularly in developing countries and vulnerable regions.

 Three New Entrants in UNESCO Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 Three important Indian documentary heritage works — the Mahabharata , Kautilya's Arthashastra and Kalhana's Rajatarangini — have been inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register .    
 Key Points:   
 Three Indian Manuscripts Recognised by UNESCO   
 The three inscriptions represent India's traditions of epic literature, historical writing, philosophy and statecraft .   
 Mahabharata Manuscript   
 Official inscription: The Birch-bark (Burjapatra) Manuscript of Mahabharata — A Perennial Epic of South Asia .   
 Preserved at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (BORI), Pune, Maharashtra .   
 The manuscript represents an important witness to the old Kashmiri recension of the Mahabharata.   
 It was acquired in Kashmir in 1875 by Indologist Georg Bühler .   
 Arthashastra Manuscript   
 Official inscription: Kautilya's Arthashastra, Ancient Palm-leaf Manuscript on Governance and Statecraft .   
 Preserved at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysuru, Karnataka .   
 Traditionally attributed to Kautilya , also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta.   
 Deals with governance, administration, economics, diplomacy, taxation and military strategy.   
 Rajatarangini Manuscript   
 Official inscription: The Manuscript of Rajatarangini by Kalhana: A Twelfth-century Chronicle of Kashmir .   
 Preserved at the Oriental Research Library, Sri Pratap Singh Library Complex, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir .   
 Written by Kalhana in Sanskrit during the 12th century.   
 It is an important historical chronicle documenting the rulers, dynasties and political history of Kashmir.   
 About UNESCO's Memory of the World Programme   
 Launch: UNESCO launched the Memory of the World Programme in 1992 .   
 Objective: To preserve and improve access to the world's significant documentary heritage.   
 Documentary heritage includes:   
 Manuscripts and rare books.   
 Historical documents and archival records.   
 Photographs and maps.   
 Films, sound recordings and other documentary materials.   
 Major objectives:   
 Preservation: Protect documentary heritage from deterioration, destruction and loss.   
 Accessibility: Improve public access to significant historical records.   
 Awareness: Promote understanding of the cultural and historical importance of documentary heritage.   
 International cooperation: Encourage collaboration among countries and institutions.   
 Three Registers under the Memory of the World Programme   
 International Register: Recognises documentary heritage of global significance.   
 Regional Register: Recognises documentary heritage of importance to a particular geographical region.   
 National Register: Identifies and promotes documentary heritage of national significance.   
 Role of IGNCA   
 Full Name: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.   
 Administrative association: Ministry of Culture, Government of India.   
 Role in the recognition: IGNCA played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three manuscripts.   
 Major functions:   
 Promoting research and documentation of India's cultural heritage.   
 Supporting the preservation and conservation of manuscripts.   
 Facilitating international recognition of India's documentary heritage.   
 Encouraging research and cooperation in the field of arts and culture.   
 Significance of the Recognition   
 Cultural Diplomacy: Strengthens international recognition of India's literary, historical and intellectual traditions.   
 Historical Research: Encourages scholarly research into India's historical sources and manuscript traditions.   
 Manuscript Conservation: Highlights the importance of preserving rare manuscripts and traditional writing materials.

 Ministry of Railways Wins PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The Ministry of Railways received the PM Surya Ghar Excellence Award 2026 for securing the top position among Central Ministries and Departments in the category of “Maximum Buildings Solarized by Central Ministries/Departments” under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana.    
 Key Points:   
 Key Achievements of the Ministry of Railways   
 Buildings identified: 15,868 feasible railway buildings have been identified across India for rooftop solar installations.   
 Buildings solarised: 12,495 buildings have been equipped with rooftop solar systems.   
 Progress: Approximately 79% of the identified feasible buildings have been solarised.   
 Installed capacity: The Ministry has commissioned 351 MW of rooftop solar capacity against a target of 424 MW.   
 Completion target: The Ministry aims to solarise all remaining feasible railway buildings by March 2027 .   
 National Progress in Rooftop Solarisation   
 Coverage: Across 77 Central Ministries and Departments:   
 39,135 buildings have been identified as suitable for rooftop solar installations.   
 25,984 buildings have been solarised.   
 Overall achievement stands at approximately 66% .   
 Railways' contribution: The Ministry of Railways has made a significant contribution to the overall rooftop solarisation of government buildings.   
 About PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana   
 Launch: The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2024 .   
 Implementing Ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).   
 Objective: To promote rooftop solar installations in residential households across the country.   
 Target: Installation of rooftop solar systems in one crore households .   
 Electricity benefit: The scheme aims to enable eligible households to receive up to 300 units of free electricity per month through rooftop solar generation.   
 Financial assistance: Central Financial Assistance is provided to eligible residential consumers for installing rooftop solar systems.   
 National Portal: The scheme uses an online portal to facilitate applications, vendor selection, installation and subsidy processing.   
 Significance of Rooftop Solarisation in Indian Railways   
 Clean Energy Transition: Reduces dependence on conventional electricity generated from fossil fuels.   
 Energy Cost Reduction: Helps reduce electricity expenditure across railway establishments.   
 Efficient Infrastructure: Utilises available rooftop space in railway buildings for decentralised electricity generation.   
 Environmental Sustainability: Contributes to reducing carbon emissions associated with electricity consumption.   
 Energy Security: Promotes greater use of renewable energy in railway operations and infrastructure.
